info.title: SOS Allert Backend API
info.description:
HTTP API for the SOS Allert life-safety backend, used by the web frontend.

Authentication: every protected endpoint expects the raw session token returned by `POST /api/users/_login` in the `Authorization` header. Do not prefix it with `Bearer `. Guest endpoints are `POST /api/users`, `POST /api/users/_login`, and `GET /metrics`.

Response envelope: success responses are `{"data": ...}` and, for paginated lists, also `{"paging": {...}}`. Errors are rendered by the global error handler as `{"errors": "<message>"}` with the matching HTTP status.

Live tracking uses a WebSocket at `ws://localhost:3000/ws/sos/{alertId}/track?token=<token>`. OpenAPI 3.0 cannot describe WebSocket frames; see `api/api.md` for the message contract.

post.description: Register a new user. Guests only. Rate limited per client IP: 5 attempts/minute, then a 15-minute lockout (`429` + `Retry-After`).

delete.description: Log out the authenticated user by clearing the stored session token.

post.description: Authenticate a user. The returned token is the raw value for the `Authorization` header on protected calls. Rate limited per client IP together with registration: 5 attempts/minute, then a 15-minute lockout (`429` + `Retry-After`).

patch.description:
Update the authenticated user's profile. All fields are optional; omitted fields are left unchanged.

- `safe_pin` is a 4-digit numeric PIN, stored as a bcrypt hash. It is required to cancel an SOS.
- `fcm_token` / `apns_token` register device push tokens so the user can receive SOS notifications.

post.description: Create a contact owned by the authenticated user.

get.description: List the authenticated user's contacts with optional filters and pagination. `name` matches first or last name with a `LIKE` search.
Get one contact owned by the authenticated user.

put.description: Replace a contact. `first_name` is required; the other fields may be empty.

delete.description: Delete a contact owned by the authenticated user.

post.description: Create an address under a contact owned by the authenticated user.

get.description: List all addresses of a contact owned by the authenticated user.
Get one address of a contact owned by the authenticated user.

put.description: Replace an address. All address fields are optional.

delete.description: Delete an address from a contact owned by the authenticated user.

get.description: Get the authenticated user's last heartbeat from Redis GEO plus the `last_seen` timestamp. Returns `404` when the user has never sent one. `stale` is `true` when `last_seen` is missing or older than 2 minutes (the same threshold used for SOS fan-out).

put.description: Send a location heartbeat. Coordinates are written to Redis GEO (`users:locations`) and the last-seen timestamp to `users:last_seen`. The same heartbeat upserts one historical row per user into MySQL `locations`. Users older than 2 minutes are excluded from SOS fan-out and the nearby endpoint, so clients should call this at least every 2 minutes while active.

get.description: List active users within `radius_m` of the authenticated user's last heartbeat. The requester must have a heartbeat (`404` otherwise). The requester and users whose `last_seen` is older than 2 minutes are excluded. Results are capped at 50, nearest first, and coordinates are rounded to ~100 m (`masked: true`) so the endpoint never exposes a precise home/office position.

post.description:
Trigger an SOS incident. The request body is optional: when coordinates are omitted, the sender's last Redis GEO position is used.

- `X-Idempotency-Key` deduplicates retried submissions for 5 minutes.
- Rate limit: `sos.rate_limit_per_hour` triggers per user per hour (default 3); HTTP 429 beyond that, with the active limit quoted in the message. The backend can turn it off with `sos.rate_limit_disabled: true` (default false).
- `description` feeds optional AI triage (fail-open). `emergency_type` sent explicitly wins over the classifier.
- `severity`/`summary` (from `POST /api/sos/classify`) also win, so an audio-classified incident fans out with the right radius on the first wave.
- A clip transcribed after the trigger that raises the severity widens the fan-out to the new radius; only the newly reached responders are notified.
- The response returns `201 Created`.

Recipients are chosen from nearby active users with adaptive radius (1/2/5 km, capped at 50) plus the sender's emergency contacts.

parameters.name: X-Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated UUID used to deduplicate retries.

post.description: Classify a short audio clip before triggering an SOS. Nothing is persisted. The response carries the audio-derived `emergency_type`, `severity` and `summary`; send them in the `POST /api/sos` body so the first fan-out already uses the audio classification (explicit values win over the description triage, and severity selects the adaptive radius). `400` for non-audio or audio above 25 MB, `503` when `ai.stt` is not configured, `502` when the provider fails.

200.description: Audio classified. `transcription_status` may be `empty` with no triage when no speech was detected.

503.description: Speech-to-text is not configured (`ai.stt.enabled` false or missing API key).

get.description: List the authenticated user's active incidents (status `TRIGGERED` or `ACKNOWLEDGED`). Useful for cold-start sync.
Responder inbox: incidents for which a push notification was delivered to the authenticated user.
Get incident detail. Any authenticated user may fetch it, but coordinates are masked (~100 m) unless the requester is the sender or a recorded responder; `masked` is `true` when masking applies.

post.description: Cancel a false alarm. Requires the authenticated sender's 4-digit safe PIN (`PATCH /api/users/_current` with `safe_pin`).

Move an incident from `TRIGGERED` to `ACKNOWLEDGED`. Any authenticated user who knows the alert id can acknowledge; acknowledging an already acknowledged incident is idempotent. The returned detail is built from the caller's perspective: coordinates are masked unless the caller is the sender or a recorded responder.
Resolve an incident. Only the sender may resolve it.

Respond to an incident as an authenticated user other than the sender. The backend computes distance and ETA from the responder's coordinates to the victim, records the response, and moves a `TRIGGERED` incident to `ACKNOWLEDGED`.

get.description: List the recorded trajectory of an incident (sender or responder).

post.description: Append one position to the incident trajectory. Only the sender can add breadcrumbs to an active incident. The equivalent WebSocket frame reports/broadcasts the same data live.

get.description: List media uploaded for an incident (sender or responder).

post.description: Upload one media file to an active incident. Sender only. Content type must be `audio/*` or `video/*`, max 50 MB. The backend stores it in the configured storage backend. Audio up to 25 MB is sent to the configured speech-to-text provider (Groq/OpenAI-compatible Whisper); the transcript feeds triage, updates the alert classification, and is returned in the response. STT/triage failures are fail-open: the media is still stored and `transcription_status` reports the outcome. If the transcript raises the incident severity, the responder fan-out widens to the larger radius (only newly reached responders are notified, still respecting the trigger grace period) and the response reports `escalated`/`recipients_added`.

200.description: Media stored, with transcript/triage when audio transcription succeeds.

get.description: Stream one media file (sender or responder). Success returns the raw file bytes with the original `Content-Type` and an inline `Content-Disposition`, not a JSON envelope.
List the authenticated user's Tier-1 emergency contacts. These are separate from the generic contacts used by the Contact API.

post.description: Create a Tier-1 emergency contact. The backend SMS/voice fallback uses this list.

get.description: Prometheus metrics in text exposition format. Guest endpoint. Includes `sos_dispatch_latency_ms`, `push_delivery_failures_total`, and `active_sos_count`.
VAPID public key the browser needs to create a push subscription. `503` when `webpush.enabled` is false or the key pair is missing.
List the authenticated user's stored browser push subscriptions.

post.description: Store a browser push subscription. `endpoint` is unique, so re-subscribing the same browser upserts the row (and re-points it at the current user).

delete.description: Remove one of the caller's subscriptions by endpoint. Unknown endpoints are a no-op (`200`) so the call is idempotent.

RawToken.name: Authorization
RawToken.description: Raw session token returned by POST /api/users/_login. Do not add a `Bearer ` prefix.

BadRequest.description: Invalid JSON, missing/invalid field, or invalid path id.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated user is not allowed to perform this action.

NotFound.description: Resource does not exist or is not owned by the authenticated user.

Conflict.description: Duplicate resource or invalid alert status transition.

PreconditionFailed.description: Required precondition is not configured (safe PIN or media storage).

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded. Auth routes allow 5 attempts/minute per client IP, then a 15-minute lockout; SOS allows 3 triggers/hour per user.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the caller may retry.

safe_pin.description: 4-digit numeric PIN. Stored as a bcrypt hash.

UserResponse.description: Profile fields. `token` is only present in the login response; other fields are omitted when empty.

last_seen.description: Epoch milliseconds; 0 when the timestamp is unavailable.

stale.description: True when last_seen is missing or older than 2 minutes.

distance_m.description: Distance from the requester in meters.

TriggerSOSRequest.description: All fields are optional. Coordinates fall back to the sender's last Redis GEO position.

description.description: Free text fed to optional AI triage.

severity.description: Pre-trigger classification from POST /api/sos/classify. Wins over the description triage and selects the adaptive fan-out radius.

summary.description: Pre-trigger summary from POST /api/sos/classify; quoted in the push body.

ClassifyResponse.description: Result of POST /api/sos/classify; nothing is persisted.

masked.description: True when coordinates are rounded (~100 m) for a viewer who is neither sender nor responder.

url.description: Authenticated download path; send the raw token in the Authorization header.

transcript.description: Speech-to-text result for audio evidence. Omitted when transcription did not produce text.

transcription_status.description: disabled = no STT provider or non-audio; too_large = audio above the 25 MB transcription limit; completed = transcript available; empty = no speech detected; failed = provider error (media is still stored).

transcribed_at.description: Epoch milliseconds when STT was attempted.

escalated.description: True when the transcript raised the incident severity enough to widen the responder fan-out to a larger radius.

recipients_added.description: Number of newly reached responders notified because of the escalation. Original recipients are never re-notified.

endpoint.description: PushSubscription.endpoint from the browser Push API.
